fixes.explanation: Not quite, baker. Moses says he's a hundred and twenty years old and no longer able to come and go. Then he tells Israel the LORD said to him, “You shall not cross the Jordan.” The one who crosses ahead of the people is the LORD Himself, and Joshua goes too.

Inheritance is right. Moses says the land is the one the LORD swore to their fathers, and Joshua will give it to the people as an inheritance. That's something handed down, and here it rests on what the LORD swore. Joshua's job is to go with the people and give it to them, and the LORD Himself goes before him (Deuteronomy 31:8).

Right. Moses gave it to “…the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.” So the law went to the ones who carried the ark and to the ones who led the community. Moses wrote it down first, so they had real pages in their hands. That's a solid team to trust with it.

That's right. Moses says their children who don't know the law will listen and learn to fear the LORD your God, “…as long as you live in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.” The reading in verse 12 gathers everyone: men, women, children, and the foreigners within your gates. So the children aren't left out of the room. They're right there in the crowd, listening.

Joshua isn't in that question, baker. The LORD says the people will ask, “Have not these disasters come upon us because our God is no longer with us?” Notice where they point. It's not at a leader or a route, but at God being no longer with them. I think that's a heavy question to hear ahead of time.

Yes. The LORD tells Moses to write the song down, teach it to the Israelites and have them recite it, “…so that it may be a witness for Me against them.” That's the whole job of the song. Later the LORD says it “…will not be forgotten from the lips of their descendants.” So it's meant to be on their lips for a long time, standing as a witness.

I can picture the party, and I'd have the cookies out already. But that's not the job the LORD gives this song. He tells Moses to write it down, teach it to the Israelites and have them recite it. The reason He gives is “…so that it may be a witness for Me against them.” Nothing here says it's for crossing the Jordan.

That's right. The LORD says this song “…will not be forgotten from the lips of their descendants.” So it doesn't fade after one generation. It's meant to be handed down the line. Moses wrote it down and taught it to the Israelites that very day (Deuteronomy 31:22).

Mount Ebal is a fine mountain, but it doesn't come up in these verses. Moses is talking to the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant. He tells them to place the book “…beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, so that it may remain there as a witness against you.” So the book's spot is right next to the ark.

That's it. Moses says, “Assemble before me all the elders of your tribes and all your officers…” He wants them gathered so that he may speak these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth to witness against them. So he's speaking to Israel's own leaders. They're the ones who will have to carry the words forward.

Yes. Moses says, “…after my death you will become utterly corrupt and turn from the path I have commanded you.” The path is the one he gave them. I think those are heavy words to say to people he has led. He adds that in the days to come, disaster will befall them because they will do evil in the sight of the LORD.
